result.topic_en: Change of variables from (p,q) to (t,T) via linear differentials and computation of the mixed second derivative of log m with respect to t and T, in the context of the theory of curved surfaces.
result.transcription:
$dt = a\,dp + b\,dq$ \quad $aB - bA = h$
$dT = A\,dp + B\,dq$
$h\,dp = B\,dt - b\,dT$
$h\,dq = -A\,dt + a\,dT$
$\frac{dh}{dT} = [-\frac{dh}{h\,dp}-] - \frac{b}{h}\frac{dh}{dp} + \frac{a}{h}\frac{dh}{dq}$
$\frac{d\log m}{dt} = [-B\frac{dm}{h\,dp} - A\frac{dm}{h\,dq}-] \frac{B}{hm}\cdot\frac{dm}{dp} - \frac{A}{hm}\cdot\frac{dm}{dq}$
$\frac{dd\log m}{dt\,dT} = -\frac{b\,dB}{hh\,dp}\cdot\frac{dm}{m\,dp} + \frac{b\,dA}{hh\,dp}\frac{dm}{m\,dq}$
$+ \frac{a\,dB}{hh\,dq}\frac{dm}{m\,dp} - \frac{a\,dA}{hh\,dq}\cdot\frac{dm}{m\,dq}$
$+ \frac{1}{hh}\left(A\frac{dm}{m\,dq} - B\frac{dm}{m\,dp}\right)\left\{-\frac{b}{h}\left\{\begin{array}{l}a'B - b'A\\ +aB' - bA'\end{array}\right\} + \frac{a}{h}\left\{\begin{array}{l}b'B - c'A\\ +aC' - bB'\end{array}\right\}\right\}$
$+ \frac{1}{h^3}\left\{A\frac{dm}{dq} - B\frac{dm}{dp}\right\}\left\{\begin{array}{l}A(ac' - bb')\\ +B(ab' - ba')\\ +A'bb - 2B'ab + C'aa\end{array}\right\}$
$+ \frac{B}{hh}\left\{-b\frac{ddm}{dp^2} + a\frac{ddm}{dp\,dq}\right\}$
$+ \frac{A}{hh}\left\{b\frac{ddm}{dp\,dq} - a\frac{ddm}{dq^2}\right\}$
